The bedroom door slammed so hard in the Madrid apartment that a photo fell off the hallway wall. 'You never let me do ANYTHING!' Leila shouted through it, because Rafael had said no to the midnight concert.
Rafael stood in the hallway, picking up the glass. His chest was tight. He felt like a doormat and a villain at the same time.
He didn't shout back. He knocked once and spoke to the door. 'I can hear you're really angry. Slamming isn't okay, because things break. I'm here when you're ready.'
Forty minutes later Leila came into the kitchen, eyes puffy. 'Sorry about the photo.'
Rafael made two hot chocolates. 'Now tell me about the concert. Properly.' He listened. The answer was still no, but together they found a Saturday afternoon show instead.

qa.q: What fell off the hallway wall?
qa.a: A photo fell off the hallway wall when the door slammed.

qa.q: How did Rafael feel standing in the hallway picking up the glass?
qa.a: He felt tense and torn, his chest tight, as if he were a doormat and a villain at the same time.

qa.q: What choice did Rafael make that held the limit and kept connection?
qa.a: He stayed calm, named Leila's anger, said slamming isn't okay, and waited to talk properly over hot chocolate once Leila had settled.

qa.q: How might Leila feel when Rafael still says no but helps find another show?
qa.a: Leila may still be disappointed but feel heard and respected, since he listened properly and offered a real alternative.

grounding: Shows an adult facing a teenager's slammed door and outburst, staying calm, holding a limit on behaviour and talking after feelings settle.

passage:
On parents' day at the school, Darshan had taken leave from his shop job to come, because Ma was on night shift. The class teacher had barely said 'maths has dropped' when Mridul shoved back his chair, shouted, 'Everyone's always on my case!' and stormed into the corridor, kicking a bench on the way.
Darshan felt heat rise in his face. He had given up a day's pay for this.
He followed and kept his voice low. 'You can be angry. You can't kick things or yell at your teacher. Sit here with me till you're ready.'
Mridul stared at the noticeboard for ten minutes. Then, quietly: 'I'm scared I'll fail, bhaiya.'
In the canteen afterwards, over two samosas, they talked properly. Then Darshan walked him back in to apologise to the teacher.

qa.q: Why had Darshan taken leave from his shop job?
qa.a: Because Ma was on night shift, so he came to parents' day.

qa.q: What did Darshan feel when Mridul stormed out, and why?
qa.a: He felt heat rise in his face, hurt and taken for granted, since he had given up a day's pay to be there.

qa.q: What choice did Darshan make that held a limit and kept connection?
qa.a: He stayed calm, said anger is fine but kicking and yelling aren't, sat with Mridul till he settled, and then talked over samosas.

qa.q: What might Mridul's outburst have been hiding?
qa.a: Fear: Mridul admitted being scared of failing, which came out as anger at everyone being on his case.

grounding: Shows an older brother facing a teenager's outburst, feeling walked on, yet staying calm, holding a limit and talking once feelings settle.
